problem:
If $A={8,9}$ and $B={x,y},$ which of the following elements belong to $A\times B\times A?$

- $(9,9,y)$
- $(8,x,y)$
- $(9,y,8)$

feedback.problem:
If $A={0,1,2}$ and $B={x,y},$ which of the following elements belong to $(A\times B)\times A?$

- $(1,y,2)$
- $((1,y),2)$
- $((y,1),y)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

In this case, $A\times B$ consists of every combination of ${0,1,2}$ with ${x,y},$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/077da578323a686ecf0e07cf0a56030fa4ce128a74d408af95b8a3027ad13f28.png)

Hence, the set $A\times B$ is given by

$$
A\times B={(0,x),(0,y),(1,x),(1,y),(2,x),(2,y)}.
$$

Note that 

$$
|A\times B|=|A|\cdot |B|=3\cdot 2=6.
$$

Now, the Cartesian product

$$
(A\times B)\times A
$$

consists of every combination of $A\times B$ and $A,$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/3a14abffc755dcfccce2d410ea18fbcae42d4afe2fbeffd81e1a291bc9d4968e.png)

Note that 

$$
|(A\times B)\times A|=|A\times B|\cdot |A|=6\cdot 3=18.
$$

From the given options, we see that only $((1,y),2)\in (A\times B)\times A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
